idiom_name: async generator over page fetches (for await...of)
implementation_notes: On the client side the anonymous callback chain collapses into an async generator: async function* awaits each page, yields the items, updates the continuation token from the response and stops when it is absent, and callers use for await...of - async generator functions conform to the async iterable protocol, so the loop is language-level (MDN). Serving the endpoint still means hand-writing the keyset query and token codec (Buffer.from(...).toString('base64url')); SDKs such as stripe-node make the consuming side library-provided (autoPagingEach, for-await over list objects), and the classic callback form is only justified on legacy runtimes without async iteration.
pitfalls: The pinned filter/order parameters must be captured once when the generator starts: spreading live caller options into every request lets a mid-iteration change silently return pages of a different sequence.

A server that echoes the same token back produces an infinite loop, and wrapping yields in a try/catch that swallows AbortError breaks cancellation - treat a non-advancing token as an error and keep cancellation errors flowing.
